question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

Our legal system must frame proper legal rules for __juvenile __criminals.
solution:
The correct answer is 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"juvenile"** means a young person or relating to young people. (किशोर)

 
 
• **Example:** The juvenile was sent to a correctional facility instead of a prison.
 
 
 
• **"Young"** refers to someone who is in the early stage of life, not old. (युवा)
 
 
• **Example:** The young athlete won several medals in the competition.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the appropriate word to substitute "juvenile" is "young".

Therefore, the correct answer is 4 i.e., **young**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Senile** (वृद्ध): Relating to or showing characteristics of old age, especially with regard to loss of cognitive abilities.

 
 
• **Example:** The senile man often forgot where he left his keys.
 
 
 
• **Dotage** (मूर्खतापूर्ण अवस्था): The period of life in which a person is old and weak.
 
 
• **Example:** In his dotage, he became very forgetful and dependent on others.
 
 
 
• **Old** (पुराना): Having lived for a long time, no longer young.
 
 
• **Example:** The old man shared many stories from his youth.
